title: Rapid rollback rehearsal and chaos simulation handoff
summary: Redwood-led rehearsal to validate rollback procedures after last week's edge cache eviction wave. Agreed on a short rollback playbook, telemetry checks, and a customer-exec chaos sim scheduled. Security wanted KMS audit and SSO caveats clarified. Next step: SE to run a dry-run and share runbook updates and benchmark script.
next_steps: Samir to share updated rollback runbook and playbook slides by 2026-02-23
BlueFork to provide a sample traffic window for dry-run by 2026-02-21
Schedule chaos sim with BlueFork on 2026-02-26 (2h)
Priya to confirm KMS rotation policy artifacts and SOC2 audit reference by 2026-02-22
action_items: Samir Patel: produce and share rollback checklist + playbook (due: 2026-02-23)
Lina Chen: send traffic window and recent alert spikes (due: 2026-02-21)
Rae Kim: coordinate chaos sim calendar invite and runbook owners (due: 2026-02-20)
Priya Nandakumar: attach KMS audit notes and SSO config constraints (due: 2026-02-22)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-19 15:00 PST — duration ~52 minutes. Attendees: Marta, Samir, Rae (Redwood) — Lina, Marcus, Priya, Diego (BlueFork).

[00:00] Marta: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we wanted to use this call to run through the rapid rollback rehearsal after that eviction wave last week, and hand off the chaos sim plan. 
[00:18] Lina: thanks Marta, yeah last week was rough, we saw big token backpressure and KV cache thrash — some of our endpoints started timing out. 
[00:30] Samir: quick correction, I think some of the transcripts flagged it as "KV cash" last time, it's KV cache, sorry, but yes we saw eviction wave on the edge caches. 
[00:45] Marcus: the important bit for us is minimizing blast radius. We want an automated rollback that restores stable model variant and ramps requests down to the dedicated pool, or back to older quantized variant. 
[01:05] Mae? (crosstalk) 
[01:12] Marta: right — today we'll cover the short rollback playbook (2–3 steps), the telemetry gates to verify safety, and the chaos sim steps. Also quick security checklist around KMS/SSO during rollback. 
[01:30] Priya: from security's perspective we're mainly concerned about key access during active rollbacks and the fact that we rotate KMS keys monthly — want to ensure logs retained and rotation doesn't interrupt the rollback path. 
[01:48] Samir: noted. We'll include KMS key-binding checks — preflight — and we can add an explicit audit-log ingestion step so your SIEM sees the rollback events. 
[02:05] Diego: can you clarify the model fallback? We have hosted calls that should switch to a lower-capacity model variant, is that automatic? 
[02:20] Samir: short answer: yes if you enable the fallback routing policy, requests will be routed to the pinned compatible variant. For the rehearsal we recommend manual trigger then automatic canary. 
[02:40] [02:40] Samir: I'll walk through the runbook now. Step 1 — detect: define detection thresholds; we recommend token latency P99 > 800ms and queue depth > 50 for 3 minutes. Step 2 — preflight: run telemetry checks (KV hits, GPU memory, kernel failures). Step 3 — trigger rollback: switch traffic to stable model ID and optionally force a cache warm-up. Step 4 — verify: run synthetic traffic and check SLO gates. Step 5 — escalate if gates fail. 
[03:30] Marcus: those thresholds seem OK but we want a lower P99 threshold during peak windows. 
[03:45] Marta: that's fine we make thresholds configable per route. We'll include a sample override for peak windows in the doc. 
[04:05] Rae: also adding a step for a slow drain of long-lived connections — we've seen connections get into half-closed state during a rollback and cause evictions. 
[04:25] [04:25] Lina: there's also the issue of stale KV entries after the eviction wave. We had some KV cache corruption; not sure if it was TTL mismatch or replication lag. 
[04:45] Samir: our hypothesis: a TTL/serialization mismatch between edge cache and primary key-value store during rapid eviction, compounded by concurrent warmup jobs. We've reproduced a similar pattern in our infra lab but results were noisy. 
[05:10] Priya: any PII exposure risk during rollback? We mask tokens, but we need explicit confirmation. 
[05:24] Samir: short answer: no PII should be emitted — but we'll include an audit step to validate no protected fields were altered. We'll add the explicit masking verification in the runbook and retention notes for audit logs. 
[05:42] [05:42] Diego: let's talk about chaos sim. We want to rehearse under a controlled window and see how automatic fallback behaves. 
[06:00] Marta: proposed plan: 1) BlueFork provides a 2h low-risk traffic window, 2) Redwood runs controlled eviction simulation (synthetic TTL spike + warmup suppression), 3) trigger automated rollback and measure recovery time and token cost delta, 4) review findings and update playbook. 
[06:30] Marcus: that timeline works. Can you schedule it next week? 
[06:36] Rae: we proposed 2026-02-26 10:00–12:00 PT in the doc, I'll send invite. 
[06:45] [06:45] Priya: what's the rollback fallback for SSO during the sim? If the control plane is unavailable SSO assertions might fail. 
[06:58] Samir: we have a fallback auth path — short-lived API tokens incident-mode — but it requires pre-approval and rotating API key stored in your KMS. We'll document the steps and permissions required. 
[07:18] Lina: can you also include the exact Cloud IAM roles needed so our infra team can pre-provision? 
[07:30] Samir: yes, we'll add a Roles matrix. 
[07:40] [07:40] Marta: let's drill into the telemetry checks we want in the runbook. Who owns which metric for go/no-go? 
[07:55] Marcus: BlueFork owns origin error spikes and custom business metrics; Redwood owns token latency, GPU eviction metrics, and KV hit ratio. 
[08:10] Samir: we'll add a gating dashboard template with explicit slices and alert IDs. 
[08:22] Rae: quick note — make sure the synthetic traffic includes a mix of short and long contexts so we exercise KV cache. 
[08:35] [08:35] Lina: last time our long contexts were the ones that tripped memory growth and caused eviction. 
[08:45] Samir: we'll include a long-context stress script; I have a small benchmark script that simulates user sessions with growing sequence lengths — I'll share the repo link in the followup. 
[09:05] Diego: how do we validate the cache warmup after rollback? 
[09:12] Samir: step: after rollback, we run a controlled warmup that hits primary prefixes and KV entries for 15 minutes with low ramp. We'll measure hit ratio and tail latencies. If hit ratio < 70% after warmup we consider rollback partial and continue warmup or revert. 
[09:36] Priya: that 70% threshold seems reasonable. 
[09:45] [09:45] Marta: security items — Priya what additional artifacts do you need? 
[09:53] Priya: KMS rotation policy excerpts, a list of audit log retention windows (especially for the rollback period), and confirmation that rollback events are stamped with immutable IDs so SIEM can correlate. 
[10:11] Samir: we'll add immutable correlation IDs to each rollback event and include sample log lines. 
[10:22] [10:22] Marcus: what about the canary step — do we prefer traffic percentage ramp or token-per-second cap? 
[10:32] Samir: we recommend a percentage ramp then a TPS cap once canary looks healthy. Example: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% with 5 minute observation windows. 
[10:52] Lina: I'd rather have a slightly shorter first observation window during low traffic. 
[11:00] Rae: we can parameterize windows in the playbook. 
[11:10] [11:10] Marta: ok let's talk about failure modes — if rollback fails to reduce latency within 10 minutes, what's the escalation path? 
[11:22] Samir: escalate to OOO (oncall) + open emergency ticket to shift traffic to dedicated pool; optional manual model swap to a quantized variant we have in reserve. 
[11:40] Diego: how long does a manual model swap take? 
[11:46] Samir: typical swap with cache warmup ~12–18 minutes, depending on model size and warmup aggressiveness. If you need sub-10m then dedicated pool redirection is faster but costlier. 
[12:05] [12:05] Priya: cost vs latency is the tradeoff we accept in emergencies. We want the policy to be clear. 
[12:15] Marta: we'll include cost estimates for each path so your execs can sign off. 
[12:26] [12:26] Marcus: any surprises from your lab reproduction? 
[12:32] Samir: reproduction showed a race between eviction and warmup threads where both tried to write back prefixes simultaneously causing a thrash loop. Fix candidates: serialized warmup or backoff and stronger lease on KV writes. We'll include mitigation tasks. 
[12:55] Rae: we'll propose a short-term mitigation (serialized warmup) and a mid-term improvement (write-lease and TTL normalization). 
[13:10] [13:10] Lina: timeline expectations? 
[13:16] Martha? (laughter) 
[13:20] Samir: short-term mitigation tested in our lab in 72 hours, mid-term change target 4–6 weeks depending on customer testing. 
[13:33] Priya: the mid-term change will need security review too. 
[13:40] [13:40] Marta: ok — let's finalize the chaos sim specifics. We'll run the dry-run scenario including synthetic eviction + warmup suppression and then trigger rollback with the runbook. We'll collect metrics and produce a short RCA/lessons doc. 
[14:02] Diego: can Redwood own the run and BlueFork observe? 
[14:10] Rae: yes, Redwood can execute in coordination; BlueFork controls times and can abort at any time. 
[14:20] [14:20] Marta: quick recap of action owners — Samir will share the runbook and the benchmark repo, Rae will send invites, Lina will provide traffic window, Priya will provide KMS/audit artifacts. 
[14:40] Marcus: sounds good. 
[14:48] [14:48] Samir: one more note — we'll include a brief script that converts run metrics to the SLO gating format you already have in your incident dashboard. 
[15:00] Lina: that's helpful. 
[15:08] [15:08] Marta: any other open questions? 
[15:12] Marcus: only minor ask — include competitor fallbacks we evaluated for exec context. 
[15:21] Marta: we'll include a short section comparing tradeoffs vs AtlasAI and CloudServe (latency, cost, integration friction). 
[15:34] Priya: thanks all. 
[15:38] [15:38] Marta: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the runbook link and RD. End of call.

Post-call notes: Redwood to include canary step templates, role matrix, KMS audit snippets, and the benchmark script repo. Customer to pick a 2h window and confirm abort criteria.
